Gene Description

CTNNB1 encodes beta-catenin, a 781-residue armadillo-repeat protein that connects cadherin-based cell adhesion with Wnt-responsive transcription. At adherens junctions, its armadillo-repeat groove binds cadherin cytoplasmic tails and its N-terminal region recruits alpha-catenin, linking the cadherin complex to the force-responsive actin-associated junctional machinery. A regulated cytoplasmic pool binds APC and AXIN in the destruction complex, where CK1/GSK3 phosphorylation enables beta-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and turnover. Canonical Wnt signaling stabilizes beta-catenin and promotes its nuclear association with TCF/LEF factors and transcriptional coactivators, activating context-dependent target genes. It also binds nuclear receptors and other regulatory partners. Its C-terminal PDZ-binding sequence supports selected scaffold interactions, while a centrosomal pool participates in centriole cohesion. These molecular activities contribute to developmental patterning, tissue homeostasis and context-dependent proliferation or differentiation; stabilizing mutations and destruction-complex defects contribute to tumorigenesis.

Reason: The original human Ku812 experiments positively co-immunoprecipitate beta-catenin with a nuclear TCF4 pool (Figures 1E and 7A). The Methods identify anti-TCF4 clone 6H5-3 and a dominant-negative construct lacking the beta-catenin-binding domain. This is HMG TCF/LEF context; the present manufacturer record maps the named antibody to TCF7L2/Q9NQB0, although its prose also contains mixed aliases. The original insert sequence and historical reagent lot were not independently established. Thus the exact P15884/E2-2 source assertion remains unresolved, while the positive TCF-family association is retained. Neither a negative P15884-binding claim nor substitution of Q9NQB0 into the machine source is justified.

GO:0090090 negative regulation of canonical Wnt signaling pathway
IEA
GO_REF:0000107 		MARK AS OVER ANNOTATED
Summary: negative regulation of canonical Wnt signaling pathway: the source supports a related observation but not the full attributed role.
Reason: The exact mouse donor is the ComplexPortal IDA from PMID:10898789. The original Results and Discussion show ICAT disrupting beta-catenin–TCF association, reducing transcriptional reporter activity, and inhibiting Xenopus axis induction; the binding-defective and dominant-negative ICAT constructs test the inhibitor. Beta-catenin is the inhibited target in these experiments. Its association with ICAT does not itself establish that beta-catenin performs the negative regulatory step. The transferred process therefore overstates this particular evidence; this is not a claim that beta-catenin can never participate in negative feedback in another setting.

Leave membership undecided pending clarification of the experimental complex boundary; absence from an inspected assay is not evidence of absence.

Core Functions

Wnt-responsive transcriptional coactivation in the nucleus. Beta-catenin binds TCF/LEF factors and participates in chromatin-associated complexes with BCL9/PYGO, CBP/p300 and other coregulators. Its activation regions support transcription without intrinsic sequence-specific DNA-binding activity. It can dock onto preassembled coregulator scaffolds; the composition and recruitment order vary with context.

Molecular Function:
transcription coactivator activity
Directly Involved In:
canonical Wnt signaling pathway positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
Cellular Locations:
nucleus
In Complex:
beta-catenin-TCF complex
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:11751639
    beta-catenin, a dedicated coactivator of LEF/TCF enhancer-binding proteins
  • PMID:9065401
    hTcf-4 transactivates transcription only when associated with beta-catenin
  • PMID:17052462
    Stimulation of the Wnt pathway leads to the association of beta-catenin with Tcf and BCL9 in the nucleus

Cadherin-tail binding and recruitment of alpha-catenin at adherens junctions. Beta-catenin provides a structural connection within the cadherin–catenin complex that supports cadherin retention, junction assembly and cell-cell adhesion. Alpha-catenin supplies the regulated actin-associated interface; beta-catenin is not assigned its partner’s actin-binding activity.

Molecular Function:
cadherin binding
Directly Involved In:
cell-cell adhesion mediated by cadherin adherens junction assembly
Cellular Locations:
adherens junction
In Complex:
catenin complex
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:11713476
    The multifunctional protein beta-catenin is important for cell adhesion, because it binds cadherins
  • PMID:18287330
    linking the VE-cadherin junction complex to the cytoskeleton
  • PMID:18593713
    Smad7 increases the stabilized beta-catenin to form a complex with E-cadherin and stabilizes the E-cadherin-beta-catenin complex
  • PMID:22837400
    Oc_bcat has two lysine residues (homologous to positions K312 and K435 in mouse) required for the interaction of mouse β-catenin with E-cadherin

Binding alpha-catenin through the N-terminal region recruits the catenin-complex alpha subunit to the cadherin-associated junctional machinery. This distinct binding activity complements cadherin-tail recognition by the armadillo-repeat region and supports the regulated connection of the junction to the actin cytoskeleton. Alpha-catenin supplies the actin-associated interface; this core does not assign direct actin-binding activity to beta-catenin.

Molecular Function:
alpha-catenin binding
Cellular Locations:
adherens junction
In Complex:
catenin complex

  • PMID:9264463

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Can the TCF4 interaction records be reconciled at clone/accession level between E2-2 (P15884) and TCF7L2 (Q9NQB0), preserving the originally curated partner while resolving historical aliases?

Q: Which below-quantification beta-catenin PDZ-screen records represent reproducible weak interactions, and which positive alternate-domain measurements can be validated with the exact native protein products?

Q: Does beta-catenin make an experimentally separable contribution to hippocampal LTD in the GO-CAM context, beyond the PTEN-associated transcriptional changes in the currently inspected source?

Q: How do beta-catenin’s junctional and transcriptional interaction surfaces contribute to mechanical responses in human tissues, distinct from the conserved molecular mechanism measured in fly experiments?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Validate the measured and marginal PDZ contacts with defined domains and full-length proteins, then test whether disrupting the beta-catenin terminal motif changes association or localization in a relevant human cell type. Keep below-quantification records distinct from established noninteractions.

Hypothesis: Selected beta-catenin C-terminal PDZ contacts are retained in the exact full-length partner context.

Type: quantitative binding and cellular interaction assays

Notes

(CTNNB1-notes.md)

CTNNB1 (human, P35222) - curation notes

Automated deep research was unavailable (no deep-research provider keys in this
environment). These notes were written by hand from the cached publications in
publications/ (many are abstract-only; see full_text_available:), the UniProt
record, the sister reviews of human VCL, sponge VIN1 and human CDH1, and a small
UniProt/PANTHER census in CTNNB1-bioinformatics/. No -deep-research-*.md file
exists for this gene.

Core molecular functions

1. Wnt/TCF transcriptional coactivator (nuclear pool)

  • Coactivator of LEF/TCF PMID:11751639;
    PMID:11751639.
  • TCF4 activity depends on beta-catenin PMID:9065401;
    constitutive complexes in APC-/- cells PMID:9065401.
  • Structure of the TCF4-beta-catenin complex PMID:11713476.
  • BCL9-Pygopus recruitment PMID:17052462;
    PMID:11955446.
  • CBP/p300 PMID:21751375.
  • Other DNA-binding partners: FOXO PMID:15905404;
    nuclear receptors PMID:22187462.
  • ICAT blocks TCF binding but not cadherin binding PMID:12408824.

2. Cadherin and alpha-catenin binding (junctional pool)

  • Binds cadherins PMID:11713476;
    links VE-cadherin to the cytoskeleton PMID:18287330.
  • Stabilizes the E-cadherin complex PMID:18593713;
    surface E-cadherin via vinculin PMID:20086044.
  • Alpha-catenin binding through the N-terminal half PMID:7890674;
    reciprocal site on alpha-catenin PMID:9264463.

Regulation (destruction complex)

  • APC binding PMID:8638126;
    GSK3/Axin PMID:17318191.
  • SCF(beta-TrCP) recognition PMID:12820959.
  • Oncogenic stabilizing mutations PMID:9065402.

Peripheral functions

  • PDZ-binding motif PMID:17242191;
    proteome-scale PDZ affinity map PMID:36115835.
  • Centrosome PMID:18086858;
    PMID:20300119.
  • PML SUMOylation PMID:22155184.

GO-CAM

gocams/index.tsv lists one CTNNB1 activity: model 62900b6400001630 "PTEN in excitatory
hippocampal synapse long-term depression (Human)", activity
gomodel:62900b6400001630/62900b6400001715, enabled by CTNNB1 (ISS from rat RGD:70487):
GO:0003713 transcription coactivator activity, part of GO:0045944 positive regulation of
transcription by RNA polymerase II, occurring in GO:0000785 chromatin. This model is the source of the
ISS rows for chromatin, transcription coactivator activity (RGD:70487) and long-term
synaptic depression. The MF typing agrees with core function 1.

Annotation review summary (723 rows)

  • Protein binding (335 IPI rows). Following repository policy:
  • MODIFY where the partner defines a specific binding function: cadherins to cadherin
    binding, alpha-catenins to alpha-catenin binding, TCF/LEF/SOX/FOXM1/RUNX3/NF-kappaB
    and other DNA-binding factors to DNA-binding transcription factor binding, nuclear
    receptors to nuclear receptor binding, protein kinases (GSK3B, SRC, ABL1, NEK2, TNIK,
    RTKs) to protein kinase binding, PTPs to protein phosphatase binding, beta-TrCP and
    other E3s to ubiquitin protein ligase binding, PDZ proteins to PDZ domain binding,
    CBP/p300 to histone acetyltransferase binding, HDAC6 to histone deacetylase binding,
    and BCL9/BCL9L, TBL1/TBLR1, parafibromin, MLLT10, CITED1, YAP/TAZ to transcription
    coregulator binding.
  • REMOVE otherwise. This includes the destruction-complex scaffolds APC, Axin and AMER1
    (captured by the destruction complex CC rows), ICAT (captured by the beta-catenin-ICAT
    complex row) and the neurodegeneration Y2H screen PMID:32814053.
  • Two specific REMOVE cases:
    • PMID:12370829 PTPRC: the abstract reports that CD45 did not bind catenins
      PMID:12370829.
    • PMID:19433865 HDAC1/2/APPL: the association goes through Reptin
      PMID:19433865.
  • Substrate-type process rows removed (participation test): protein polyubiquitination
    and proteasome-mediated catabolism (PMID:29374064), and regulation of protein
    ubiquitination (PMID:15829978). Beta-catenin is the substrate in all three
    PMID:29374064.
  • MODIFY of non-binding rows:
  • Obsolete GO:0030331 nuclear estrogen receptor binding to GO:0016922. QuickGO
    confirms the obsolescence and gives GO:0016922 as the consider term.
  • GO:0070602 regulation of centromeric sister chromatid cohesion to GO:0030997
    regulation of centriole-centriole cohesion. The cited paper (PMID:20300119) is
    about centrosome cohesion.
  • GO:0019900 kinase binding with GSK3B to protein kinase binding.
  • Enzyme binding with HDAC6 to histone deacetylase binding.
  • UNDECIDED: GO:0045892 negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription (IMP,
    PMID:19653274). The abstract says the LEF-1 isoform effect is beta-catenin-independent
    PMID:19653274,
    and the full text is not cached.
  • Over-annotated:
  • Chromatin binding (beta-catenin has no DNA-binding domain).
  • Detection of mechanical stimulus and detection of muscle stretch.
  • Wnt signalosome.
  • Negative regulation of canonical Wnt signaling.
  • Response to xenobiotic stimulus (sulindac) and response to indole-3-methanol (both
    expression-change evidence).
  • Bicellular tight junction, focal adhesion (HDA) and extracellular exosome (HDA).
  • Non-core: the many mouse-derived developmental, neural and synaptic terms. These
    are downstream outputs of Wnt/TCF target genes or tissue-specific instances of
    junctional localization.
  • IBA rows (PAINT node PTN001153077): cadherin binding, alpha-catenin binding, catenin
    complex, adherens junction, cell-cell adhesion, transcription coactivator activity,
    canonical Wnt signaling, nucleus/cytoplasm, nuclear receptor binding, protein
    phosphatase binding and positive regulation of Pol II transcription. All accepted.
    Human CTNNB1 among the donors is expected, not circular. The donors are bilaterian
    (fly arm, worm hmp-2/bar-1/sys-1, mouse, zebrafish, human JUP).

Premetazoan evidence: ancestral vs animal-specific

Bioinformatics (CTNNB1-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md):
- PANTHER PTHR45976, the beta-catenin/Armadillo family containing CTNNB1 as SF4, has 4921
metazoan UniProt members.
- It has 0 members in choanoflagellates, Filasterea, Ichthyosporea or Dictyostelium. The
only 2 non-metazoan hits are isolated plant entries, probably contamination.
- Dictyostelium Aardvark (Q54I71) is classified in PTHR22895 "ARMADILLO REPEAT-CONTAINING
PROTEIN 6", not in the beta-catenin family.

Literature (all read in the cache):
- Beta-catenin as an animal-specific family: catenin beta is a core animal-specific
family PMID:29848444.
Wnt-pathway genes are largely absent outside animals
PMID:20883218.
- The armadillo fold is older PMID:23481191.
- Dictyostelium (Amoebozoa, an independent origin of multicellularity):
- Aardvark acts at actin-associated junctions and separately in signalling
PMID:11130075.
- The authors concluded PMID:11130075.
- The later study showed that an alpha-catenin ortholog binds Aardvark to build a
polarized epithelium without cadherins
PMID:21393547;
PMID:21393547.
- Aardvark's signalling role does not go through GSK-3, i.e. it is not Wnt-like
destruction-complex signalling
PMID:12128211.
- Classical cadherins are an animal innovation
PMID:22837400.
- The sponge beta-catenin keeps the residues that bind cadherin
PMID:22837400.
- A Y2H screen with the sponge beta-catenin recovered the sponge classical cadherin (same paper).
- Nuclear signalling is ancient within animals: cnidarian nuclear beta-catenin
specifies endoderm
PMID:14647383.
- Sponge vinculin did not bind a beta-catenin peptide
PMID:29880641.
The VCL review notes that this peptide was the alpha-catenin-binding region, so the
result does not test the human vinculin-beta-catenin N-terminal interface.

Synthesis:
- Ancestral (pre-animal), in the broad sense: an armadillo-repeat catenin working with
alpha-catenin to organize cell polarity and junctions. The evidence comes from
Dictyostelium. Whether Aardvark shares descent with beta-catenin or converged on this
role is unresolved: PANTHER does not place it in the beta-catenin family, and no
beta-catenin-family protein is classified in unicellular holozoans.
- Animal-specific:
- The beta-catenin family itself (by current classification).
- Binding of classical cadherins (the partners arise with animals, though present in
sponges).
- TCF/LEF-dependent transcriptional coactivation in Wnt signalling (TCF/LEF and Wnt are
animal-specific).
- All of the developmental, tissue and synaptic process terms.
- Both the junctional and the Wnt/TCF roles were present in the last common ancestor of
animals (sponge cadherin-binding residues; sponge Wnt-pathway components; cnidarian
nuclear beta-catenin).
- Unverified background, not cited: whether ctenophores have a TCF-coupled beta-catenin.
I did not read primary data on this.

2026-10-13: complete source-specific augmentation

This entry supplements the preserved journal above. It supersedes its older generic-binding removal policy and the source interpretations identified below. All 723 historical annotation source objects remain exact, including qualifiers, partner accessions, evidence codes and multiplicity. The current 737 API records and 736 literal TSV rows reconcile to those same 723 source keys; date-only and other literal multiplicities remain in the audit rather than being rewritten into the historical cache. No NEW annotation is proposed.

The full review now distinguishes 255 ACCEPT, 233 KEEP_AS_NON_CORE, 185 MODIFY, 44 UNDECIDED, three REMOVE and three MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED decisions. Of 335 generic protein-binding assertions, 180 receive source-supported refinements, 120 remain positive non-core interactions, 34 are unresolved and one is contradicted by its original experiment. This follows the standing project instruction in projects/CLINGEN_MENDELIAN.md under the generic-binding policy: retain supported correct interactions when no justified specific replacement is available. A partner class describes what beta-catenin binds; it does not assign that partner's catalytic activity to beta-catenin.

Molecular functions and products

The two compact core units are nuclear transcriptional coactivation and cadherin-tail binding at adherens junctions. The latter explicitly includes alpha-catenin recruitment without assigning alpha-catenin's actin-binding function to beta-catenin. Human LEF/TCF chromatin-template experiments establish cooperative beta-catenin association and transcriptional activity; absence of an intrinsic sequence-specific DNA-binding domain does not exclude partner-mediated chromatin association. ICAT can suppress transcription while the LEF–beta-catenin complex remains chromatin-bound at the tested doses, so its action is not universally simple displacement (PMID:11751639). The source's positive binding does not by itself establish the narrower current transcription-corepressor class for ICAT.

The official P35222 record supplies one displayed 781-residue product and no ALTERNATIVE PRODUCTS listing. This limited official scope is not a claim that all transcripts or experimental deletions are equivalent. Human TCF7L2 residues 8–54 and beta-catenin 134–668 were coexpressed in bacteria for the structural study, with 293-cell reporter tests (PMID:11713476). Other studies use truncations, phosphosite mutants, species-specific constructs and tagged domains; curated whole-reference ROGIDs do not establish the actual fragment sequence. The prior taxonomic census is preserved as a historical classification analysis, not a new origin-date inference. Its own limitations leave the relationship of Dictyostelium Aardvark unresolved; the actual current PAINT node placement is assessed separately.

Interaction identity, catalytic classes and quantitative screens

Historical TCF4 is an important accession ambiguity. Official P15884 is TCF4/E2-2; Q9NQB0 is TCF7L2, historically also called TCF4. Recovered original Methods and fragments frequently describe HMG TCF/LEF reagents. Eight exact P15884 pair assertions therefore remain UNDECIDED without replacing their source accessions. The PMID:25402006 experimental GST/radiolabel pair is retained with curator deference and a specific RNA polymerase II transcription-factor-binding refinement: its canonical P15884 assignment has no observed contradictory insert in the material available. Its supplementary image/insert remains unread. The biologically supported TCF/LEF complex remains ACCEPT, with the accession ambiguity explicit. A TCF7L2 quotation is not reused as proof of a distinct P15884 pair.

PMID:12370829 Figure 3B is a genuine source contradiction for the CD45 pair: the target-height beta-catenin band occurs for DEP1 D/A with pervanadate, not CD45 D/A. The original experiment uses bacterial GST catalytic-domain trapping constructs and HUVEC lysates. The positive MINT source field remains untouched; the specific assignment is REMOVE without a new NOT assertion or a universal claim that CD45 never associates with beta-catenin. A separate phosphopeptide/CD45 interaction in PMID:19167335 remains distinct.

PTPRU binding is retained while its older active-phosphatase interpretation is qualified by the later pseudophosphatase original (PMID:32591542). The historical dephosphorylation excerpt is preserved at that row as a disputed claim. It is removed as generic corroboration for unrelated phosphatase partners. PTPN23 is assessed independently: PMID:19340315 reports negative wild-type synthetic-substrate activity, whereas PMID:21724833 reports peptide turnover and E1357A lysate trapping, and PMID:29066500 reports wild-type-domain dephosphorylation of immunoprecipitated FYN relative to C1392S. These support a qualified phosphatase partner class; none proves that beta-catenin itself was dephosphorylated in the trapping assay. PTPRU's class is not transferred to PTPN23 by analogy.

The actual fragmentomics workbook contains 266 beta-catenin entries: 133 measured DAPF rows and 133 entries with blank assay fields. The tested beta-catenin tail is residues 772–781, NQLAWFDTDL, paired with isolated PDZ domains (PMID:36115835). Seventy literal records reconcile with the 27 imported generic assertions. Twelve receive PDZ-domain-binding refinement; fifteen remain UNDECIDED where the recorded domain is below quantification. Positive alternate domains are explicitly separated from a censored original-domain record. The LNX1 PDZ1 result lies only 0.00004825 above the BI 0.05 threshold, with n=2 and no reported SD; it is not robust affinity evidence for every LNX1 product. The correction concerns figure labels, not replacement of the workbook. The public index supplies compact domain/assay limits, not a raw workbook dump.

Processes, localization and performed roles

The original centrosome experiments measure gamma-tubulin-marked centrosome separation and beta-catenin phosphorylation/localization. They support regulation of centriole cohesion, not centromeric sister-chromatid cohesion (PMIDs:18086858 and 20300119). The latter cache is partial despite its true full-text flag; its missing Results/Discussion were genuinely recovered independently. The mouse source record is now traced directly, rather than described as an unavailable donor lookup. NEK2 binding has recombinant evidence; rootletin co-IP is retained without claiming personally inspected supplemental Far-Western data.

The three source-specific removals concern the CD45 assay above and two assignments treating beta-catenin's own IRF2BPL-dependent ubiquitination/turnover as work it performs (PMID:29374064). By contrast, the complete PMID:23245942 abstract explicitly describes beta-catenin bridging TAZ to beta-TrCP. That different-substrate regulatory role supports non-core regulation of ubiquitination; its full original remains inaccessible. The old own-substrate excerpt is retained alongside the new abstract anchor so that this distinction is visible. The ICAT-derived negative-Wnt assertion is over-annotated because ICAT performs inhibition and beta-catenin is its inhibited target (PMID:10898789).

Mechanical participation is not rejected merely for lacking an autonomous sensor. The molecular interface measured in fly experiments and mouse-structure simulations can support a conserved human inference, with human Y654 verified, and is retained as non-core detection of mechanical stimulus (PMID:30024850). This is not a human or muscle experiment. The specific muscle-stretch assertion from PMID:30568254 remains unresolved because expression/localization and accessible cited abstracts do not settle that endpoint.

The indole-3-carbinol study reports catenin abundance changes after 24 hours in human MCF-7 and MDA-MB-468 cells, with a proposed joint cadherin–catenin anti-invasion mechanism (PMID:10868478). The response definition permits expression changes and does not require direct sensing. GO expression guidance nevertheless permits declining an expression-only association where participation is not established (GO Consortium guide, PMC3706743, expression-study paragraph). The indole rows remain source-specific overannotations of beta-catenin's performed contribution, preserving the positive observation. Sulindac also changes beta-catenin/TCF activity and target expression, but operative Methods/Results are absent from the selected cache; that response assertion remains UNDECIDED (PMID:18291362).

Other contextual positives retain actual source scope: TRPC4 association, targeting and calcium entry depend on cell-contact state, with mouse channel constructs and human hosts distinguished (PMID:19996314); the M8P/vinculin experiments support cadherin-surface stabilization without loss of every beta-catenin partner (PMID:20086044); the antibody-specificity paper preserves controlled beta-catenin redistribution while identifying a cross-reacting nuclear antigen (PMID:19187541). The SATB1 source remains accompanied by its editorial notices, not treated as retracted or free of concerns. Corrections to PMID:22056988 and PMID:33428810 have narrower reporting scopes and do not reverse the inspected target findings.

Phylogeny, transfers and curated models

The actual 137-node PTHR45976 tree and MSA contain the exact 781-residue target PTN002511128. All 12 scoped IBDs are at on-path PTN001153077, with their recorded taxon placement preserved. Short donor lists and legitimate human self donors are not failures. The full donor and orthology records retain extensions and assay contexts; not every underlying donor paper was personally read. Missing current exact records are distinguished from functional loss, with descendant terms checked where appropriate. The seven ARBA rules were reconstructed across 1,295 condition branches; matching a branch does not settle the biological scope of its output.

All 77 cited Reactome event summations and 160 literal target paths were inspected. Beta-catenin can appear in a complex, as a phosphorylated substrate or as an input to a reaction; membership does not give it the catalyst's activity. HPA XML supports its stated plasma-membrane, junction and conditional ciliary/basal-body contexts; image-pixel inspection is not claimed.

GO-CAM 62900b6400001630 retains activity 62900b6400001715: transcription coactivator activity in chromatin, placed within positive transcription regulation and hippocampal LTD through rat RGD:70487 transfer. This corroborates the coactivator role but is not an independent human LTD experiment. The exact current rat LTD source was not reconstructed, and the inspected mouse PTEN promoter-occupancy work does not independently settle beta-catenin-specific LTD performance. The LTD row remains UNDECIDED. Likewise, cytosolic LRRK2/destruction-complex co-IP and a recruitment model do not settle direct receptor-associated Wnt-signalosome membership (PMIDs:22899650 and 24115276).

Access and preservation

The 265 historical PMID abstracts were personally read, together with the explicitly recorded selected original Methods/Results and independently attributed bounded consultations. A cache's full-text flag does not establish complete experimental access. References distinguish source identity, target support, original recovery and unread supplementary data. The immutable audit contains raw receipts, exact source joins and personal read windows; the compact public index provides reproducible public/repository locators and conclusions without copying those responses or every annotation decision.

The normal isolated fetch completed. Genuine default Falcon and bounded fallback attempts ended in timeouts without a provider report; no manual text is labeled as provider output. Historical notes, source caches, provider artifacts, bioinformatics and six history records remain preserved. Relevant supplied excerpts are retained; narrow removals correct a misleading partner/role linkage, not a blanket quotation budget. The sole newly selected external quote is the short PMID:23245942 bridge statement, used once in the annotation support.

Independent whole-review refinements

The receptor-binding comparison refines two further positive interactions to GO:0005102. PMID:21132015 reports human PTK7 intracellular-domain mapping, full-length co-immunoprecipitation in COS7 cells and endogenous Caco2 association. PMID:24960609 reports mouse Ryk full-length and uncleavable receptor association with endogenous beta-catenin in 293T cells, separately from its released intracellular domain. Neither refinement assigns kinase activity to the pseudokinase partner or agonist activity to beta-catenin. COS7 is not a human cell line; the paper's wording is not repeated as a species claim.

The final counts after these two refinements are 255 ACCEPT, 231 KEEP_AS_NON_CORE, 187 MODIFY, 44 UNDECIDED, three REMOVE and three MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED. Among the 335 generic-binding sources, 182 are refined, 118 retained as non-core, 34 unresolved and one removed. Four additional reason corrections preserve actions: B6V8E6 is the dog ortholog, and NAS/TAS neurogenesis rows and the human IMP mesenchymal-stem-cell row do not inherit the mouse-transfer wording from other annotations. All original source objects, references, products, quotations and both core functions remain unchanged.

2026-10-14: explicit alpha-catenin core and finite review follow-up

The molecular-function schema has one MF slot per core unit. Alpha-catenin binding (GO:0045294) is therefore restored as an explicit third core alongside transcriptional coactivation and cadherin binding. Its N-terminal interaction recruits the alpha subunit into junctional machinery, while alpha-catenin supplies the regulated actin-associated interface. Five existing alpha-catenin-binding annotations and eleven binding refinements already retain this function. Two existing source-exact anchors from PMID:7890674 and PMID:9264463 move from the cadherin core to the new alpha-catenin core, without duplication. Their cached abstracts explicitly report the interaction/domain mapping, but do not authenticate all assay constructs. The comparative Dictyostelium source PMID:21393547 remains relevant comparative evidence in the preserved findings and journal, not a direct human experimental anchor or a resolved origin-date claim.

The preceding statement that “both core functions remain unchanged” described only the final twelve-leaf owner refinement relative to its already two-core first draft. It did not describe the change from the historical three-core review. That earlier consolidation is now reversed at the machine-readable MF level. All prior journal text and history records remain intact; this paragraph supersedes the earlier two-core synthesis.

The optional FLYWCH1/ICAT generalization was reconsidered against both current definitions. GO:0001221 retains the non-DNA-binding coregulator/basal-machinery role; moving to that parent does not resolve the source-specific classification uncertainty. Positive FLYWCH1 binding/repression and ICAT inhibition remain explicit under their existing UNDECIDED and KEEP_AS_NON_CORE decisions. No domain-absence exclusion or negative binding assertion is introduced.

LNX1 PDZ1 remains a narrow biochemical positive under the original study’s BI threshold: 0.05004825 exceeds 0.05, but with only two measurements and no standard deviation. The source-specific precision caveat is now explicit in its reason. This differs from the fifteen below-quantification rows; no new threshold or statistical confidence is invented. The conserved mechanosensing inference remains explicitly based on fly experiments and mouse-structure simulations, not direct human or muscle assays. One duplicate bare PMID:15829978 support pointer is removed; its inherited quoted evidence and the independent PMID:23245942 TAZ-bridging support are retained.

The other nonblocking suggestions do not require broad scientific churn: source-specific HIGH relevance records remain tied to the actual asserted functions; detailed reasons carry the assay/partner distinctions behind repeated concise summaries. Earlier history is append-only; the new history can name only applicable YAML sections and mention the separate notes/evidence files in its details. Genuine provider failures remain documented, with no fabricated report or repeated provider request in this finite follow-up. All 723 source objects, actions/replacements, 360 references, official product, machine caches and prior notes are preserved.

Bioinformatics Results

(RESULTS.md)

CTNNB1: taxonomic census of the beta-catenin family (UniProt)

Script: taxon_census.py (stdlib only, UniProt REST API). Raw output: census_output.txt
(run 2026-10-01).

Question

Is the beta-catenin family (as defined by PANTHER PTHR45976 "ARMADILLO SEGMENT
POLARITY PROTEIN", which contains human CTNNB1 as PTHR45976:SF4, and InterPro
IPR013284 "Beta-catenin") found outside animals, in particular in the unicellular
holozoans (choanoflagellates, filastereans, ichthyosporeans) or in Dictyostelium?

Results

Classification Metazoa non-Metazoa Choanoflagellata Filasterea Ichthyosporea Dictyostelium
PANTHER PTHR45976 4921 2 0 0 0 0
InterPro IPR013284 4937 3 0 0 0 0
  • The two non-metazoan PTHR45976 entries are single proteins from land-plant
    genome assemblies (Sphagnum jensenii A0ABP0VBH0, Olea europaea A0A8S0TRJ0).
    No other plant has one, so these are most likely contaminating animal sequences in
    the assemblies; this was not tested here.
  • The extra IPR013284 entry is a chytrid "Vacuolar protein 8" (A0A139A5K2) that
    PANTHER puts in a different family (PTHR47249), so the InterPro signature
    picks up an unrelated ARM protein here.
  • Dictyostelium Aardvark (Q54I71), the "beta-catenin homologue" of
    PMID:11130075, is placed by PANTHER in PTHR22895 "ARMADILLO REPEAT-CONTAINING
    PROTEIN 6"    , not in the beta-catenin family.

Interpretation (limits)

  • By current HMM classifications, the beta-catenin family is restricted to animals,
    with no members in choanoflagellates, Capsaspora or ichthyosporeans. This agrees
    with gene-family reconstructions that list catenin beta as an animal-specific family
    (PMID:29848444).
  • Aardvark is an armadillo-repeat protein that works with a Dictyostelium
    alpha-catenin ortholog (PMID:21393547). Database classification does not put it
    in the beta-catenin family. Whether it is a divergent ortholog, an older ARM
    paralog, or a convergent junction protein would need a proper phylogeny of
    ARM-repeat proteins, which was not done here.
  • These are classification counts, not a phylogeny. A beta-catenin-like gene that
    is missing from UniProt or classified elsewhere would not be detected.

id: P35222
gene_symbol: CTNNB1
product_type: PROTEIN
status: DRAFT
taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:9606
  label: Homo sapiens
description: CTNNB1 encodes beta-catenin, a 781-residue armadillo-repeat protein that connects
  cadherin-based cell adhesion with Wnt-responsive transcription. At adherens junctions, its
  armadillo-repeat groove binds cadherin cytoplasmic tails and its N-terminal region recruits
  alpha-catenin, linking the cadherin complex to the force-responsive actin-associated junctional
  machinery. A regulated cytoplasmic pool binds APC and AXIN in the destruction complex, where
  CK1/GSK3 phosphorylation enables beta-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination and turnover. Canonical
  Wnt signaling stabilizes beta-catenin and promotes its nuclear association with TCF/LEF
  factors and transcriptional coactivators, activating context-dependent target genes. It
  also binds nuclear receptors and other regulatory partners. Its C-terminal PDZ-binding sequence
  supports selected scaffold interactions, while a centrosomal pool participates in centriole
  cohesion. These molecular activities contribute to developmental patterning, tissue homeostasis
  and context-dependent proliferation or differentiation; stabilizing mutations and destruction-complex
  defects contribute to tumorigenesis.

    action: MODIFY
    reason: The original study captures beta-catenin from U373-MG lysate with recombinant
      human PTPRZ1 D1 (residues 1655–2018), including the C1925S trapping construct; active

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:11751639
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9NSA3
  review:
    summary: 'protein binding: retain the positive contextual association or function.'
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: Preserve the positive ICAT/CTNNBIP1 interaction under the standing project instruction.
      The original directly demonstrates ICAT-dependent inhibition in the LEF1–beta-catenin
      chromatin system. At transcription-inhibiting concentrations, cooperative LEF1/beta-catenin
      occupancy can persist; simple competition is not an exhaustive mechanism. Inhibition
      of a coactivator does not by itself establish the more specific basal-machinery/coregulator
      role described by GO:0001221 or GO:0001222. Retaining generic binding avoids inventing
      that partner class, while rejecting neither binding nor transcriptional inhibition.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:11751639

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:16574648
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q92729
  review:
    summary: 'protein binding: retain the positive contextual association or function.'
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The original PMID:16574648 Methods, Figure 3D caption and Figure 5A/B Results
      support association of PCP-2/PTPRU with beta-catenin. Later biochemical and structural
      analysis of human Q92729-1 (PMID:32591542) identifies catalytically inactive PTPRU,
      so the old enzyme-class inference to GO:0019903 is not adequately supported. Preserve
      the positive generic binding as non-core under the project instruction, with no invented
      specific replacement; pseudophosphatase status does not negate binding. The inherited
      excerpt records the older claimed dephosphorylation; the later catalytic evidence disputes
      that clause while preserving association.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:16574648
      supporting_text: directly binds and dephosphorylates beta-catenin
    - reference_id: PMID:32591542

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:17318191
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P15884
  review:
    summary: 'protein binding: the specific source or functional scope remains unresolved.'
    action: UNDECIDED
    reason: The original human Ku812 experiments positively co-immunoprecipitate beta-catenin
      with a nuclear TCF4 pool (Figures 1E and 7A). The Methods identify anti-TCF4 clone 6H5-3
      and a dominant-negative construct lacking the beta-catenin-binding domain. This is HMG
      TCF/LEF context; the present manufacturer record maps the named antibody to TCF7L2/Q9NQB0,
      although its prose also contains mixed aliases. The original insert sequence and historical
      reagent lot were not independently established. Thus the exact P15884/E2-2 source assertion
      remains unresolved, while the positive TCF-family association is retained. Neither a
      negative P15884-binding claim nor substitution of Q9NQB0 into the machine source is
      justified.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:17318191
      supporting_text: This Y-phospho beta-catenin binds to the TCF4 transcription factor,
        thus representing a transcriptionally active pool

      PTPN23 peptide turnover and later WT-domain FYN dephosphorylation with a catalytic-cysteine

  review:
    summary: 'protein binding: refine to signaling receptor binding at the demonstrated partner
      and construct scope.'
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The source tests mouse Ryk constructs in human 293T cells: wild-type and uncleavable
      full-length Ryk co-immunoprecipitate endogenous beta-catenin, while the intracellular
      cleavage product also associates separately. Ryk is a Wnt signaling receptor with an
      inactive kinase-like domain. Signaling receptor binding captures the full-length receptor
      association without implying kinase binding, beta-catenin agonism, or equivalence between
      intact receptor and released intracellular-domain functions.'

    - reference_id: PMID:24960609

  qualifier: enables

  review:
    summary: 'protein binding: the specific source or functional scope remains unresolved.'
    action: UNDECIDED
    reason: The selected original Methods and Results specify TCF4 fragments 8-54 for beta-catenin
      binding and 326-411 for DNA binding, and a larger 8-411 construct with an internal deletion.
      This HMG TCF7L2-like architecture differs from the C-terminal bHLH domain of canonical
      P15884/E2-2. The positive beta-catenin/TCF4 assays remain valid, but they do not establish
      the literal imported P15884 partner. Preserve that machine source and record the unresolved
      accession/construct mismatch; do not invent an exact historical isoform sequence or
      infer absence of P15884 binding in other contexts.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:28051067
      supporting_text: β-catenin translocates into the nucleus, where it interacts with the
        transcription factors TCF4/LEF1 to regulate the expression of the target genes

  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:A4D2P6
  review:
    summary: 'protein binding: the specific source or functional scope remains unresolved.'
    action: UNDECIDED
    reason: The source tests the human beta-catenin C-terminal peptide 772–781 (NQLAWFDTDL)
      against isolated tagged GRID2IP PDZ domains by holdup, rather than intact cellular complexes.
      The literal positive IntAct records are recoverable, but all matching original workbook
      measurements are below the authors’ quantification threshold (composite pKd recorded
      as zero; normalized BI below 0.05). Their positive/nonnegative curation and the underlying
      quantitative result therefore remain unresolved. The paper explicitly states that below-threshold
      pairs are not established noninteractions. Preserve the source assertion and its genuine
      database records, but do not infer a validated positive PDZ contact, remove the biological
      interaction, or add a NOT qualifier from these censored measurements.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:36115835
      supporting_text: both containing PBMs that detectably bound to PDZs in our quantified
        interactome
    - reference_id: PMID:17242191
      supporting_text: such as the one between the β-catenin PDZ motif and the PDZ2 domain

      retain positive nuclear/cytosolic redistribution and Wnt-context evidence. Accept the

      junctional targeting. In HEK293 reconstitution, beta-catenin expression promotes TRPC4-dependent

    summary: 'adherens junction: supported at the stated source and biological scope.'
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The source compares beta-catenin M8P with wild type in vinculin binding and rescue
      of surface E-cadherin/junctional organization. M8P preserves cadherin and alpha-catenin
      binding but fails the vinculin-associated surface-stabilization rescue. This supports
      a structural contribution to cadherin localization/assembly rather than a knockout-only
      inference. The reported mouse beta-catenin and chick vinculin constructs are distinguished
      from human MCF10a/Caco2 cell contexts and canine MDCK lysate.

  review:
    summary: 'enzyme binding: retain the positive contextual association or function.'
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The source supports association with HDAC6 in the EGFR/beta-catenin context. Its
      current official record emphasizes nonhistone deacetylation and cautions about the historical

- term:
    id: GO:0034333
    label: adherens junction assembly
  evidence_type: IMP
  original_reference_id: PMID:20086044
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: 'adherens junction assembly: supported at the stated source and biological scope.'
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The source compares beta-catenin M8P with wild type in vinculin binding and rescue
      of surface E-cadherin/junctional organization. M8P preserves cadherin and alpha-catenin
      binding but fails the vinculin-associated surface-stabilization rescue. This supports
      a structural contribution to cadherin localization/assembly rather than a knockout-only
      inference. The reported mouse beta-catenin and chick vinculin constructs are distinguished
      from human MCF10a/Caco2 cell contexts and canine MDCK lysate.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:20086044
      supporting_text: an interaction between beta-catenin and vinculin is crucial for stabilizing
        E-cadherin at the cell surface
    - reference_id: PMID:18287330
      supporting_text: linking the VE-cadherin junction complex to the cytoskeleton

- term:
    id: GO:0050982
    label: detection of mechanical stimulus
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000117
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - ARBA:ARBA00091369
  review:
    summary: 'detection of mechanical stimulus: retain the positive contextual association
      or function.'
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: Retain contextual mechanical detection as an explicit inference to conserved human
      junctional machinery. The matching primate beta-catenin FunFam rule and molecular force-sensitive
      interface evidence support the broad assertion; the latter is a Drosophila experiment
      with mouse-structure simulations, not direct human or muscle evidence. Beta-catenin
      contributes the responsive interface rather than merely being an unrelated downstream
      substrate. The current rule genuinely matches ARBA00091369 branch(es) 1. Matching a
      rule is distinct from validating its biological scope.
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: NO_FAILURE_NON_CORE
      source_entities:
      - source_id: ARBA:ARBA00091369
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: Actual current matching condition branches 1; all predicates evaluated, with
          no unknown condition treated as true.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:30024850

  review:
    summary: 'canonical Wnt signaling pathway: supported at the stated source and biological

    label: canonical Wnt signaling pathway
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:19187541
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: 'canonical Wnt signaling pathway: supported at the stated source and biological
      scope.'
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The original antibody-specificity study distinguishes a cross-reacting nuclear
      8E7 antigen from genuine beta-catenin using deficient cells and additional antibodies.
      Its controlled HEK293T lithium response and SW480 E-cadherin-reexpression experiments
      retain positive nuclear/cytosolic redistribution and Wnt-context evidence. Accept the
      biological assertion without treating every 8E7-stained nucleus as beta-catenin or treating
      the entire study as a negative localization result.

- term:
    id: GO:0071681
    label: cellular response to indole-3-methanol
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:10868478
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: 'cellular response to indole-3-methanol: the source supports a related observation
      but not the full attributed role.'
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: The original 24-hour indole-3-carbinol experiments measure increased alpha-, beta-
      and gamma-catenin protein abundance by Western blot in human MCF-7 and MDA-MB-468 cells.
      Anti-invasion effects are associated with an increased whole cadherin–catenin complex,
      without isolating beta-catenin’s contribution to that response. The GO definition permits
      expression changes and does not require direct drug sensing; nevertheless, this source
      supports an expression association more securely than beta-catenin participation in
      the response. Retain the observation while marking this source-specific process attribution
      over-annotated.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:10868478
      supporting_text: three major catenins (alpha, beta, and gamma-catenin)

- term:
    id: GO:0090090
    label: negative regulation of canonical Wnt signaling pathway
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000107
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q02248
  - ensembl:ENSMUSP00000007130
  review:
    summary: 'negative regulation of canonical Wnt signaling pathway: the source supports
      a related observation but not the full attributed role.'
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: The exact mouse donor is the ComplexPortal IDA from PMID:10898789. The original
      Results and Discussion show ICAT disrupting beta-catenin–TCF association, reducing transcriptional
      reporter activity, and inhibiting Xenopus axis induction; the binding-defective and
      dominant-negative ICAT constructs test the inhibitor. Beta-catenin is the inhibited
      target in these experiments. Its association with ICAT does not itself establish that
      beta-catenin performs the negative regulatory step. The transferred process therefore
      overstates this particular evidence; this is not a claim that beta-catenin can never
      participate in negative feedback in another setting.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: GO_REF:0000107
    - reference_id: PMID:10898789
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: SOURCE_BAD
      source_entities:
      - source_id: UniProtKB:Q02248
        source_status: SOURCE_BAD
        comment: Resolved accession Q02248. Exact records 417244558; references PMID:10898789.
          Literal extensions retained; source experiments are not all claimed as personally
          read. The original source’s experimental scope is reassessed in the annotation reason.
- term:
    id: GO:0090279
    label: regulation of calcium ion import
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:19996314
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: 'regulation of calcium ion import: retain the positive contextual association
      or function.'
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The original HMEC-1 experiments recover TRPC4 with beta-catenin and show contact-dependent
      junctional targeting. In HEK293 reconstitution, beta-catenin expression promotes TRPC4-dependent
      calcium entry in contact-forming cells but retains channel intracellularly in isolated
      cells. Preserve this conditional association/targeting role. Mouse TRPC4 constructs,
      human cell hosts and the authors’ unresolved possibility of additional bridging scaffolds
      are distinct; the assays do not establish a purified binary interaction.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:19996314

- term:
    id: GO:1990907
    label: beta-catenin-TCF complex
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:11955446
  qualifier: part_of
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:O00512
  - UniProtKB:P15884
  review:
    summary: 'beta-catenin-TCF complex: supported at the stated source and biological scope.'
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: The current GO:1990907 definition specifies a beta-catenin complex containing
      a TCF/LEF-family member. The literal source includes P15884, whose alias ambiguity must
      remain explicit; the two matched PMID:11955446 interaction records establish BCL9 associations,
      not a resolved P15884 pair. Nevertheless, human beta-catenin/TCF-LEF complex biology
      is independently demonstrated by the recovered PMID:17875931 experiments and the previously
      read human LEF1 chromatin-complex experiments in PMID:11751639. Retain the biologically
      correct complex annotation without treating the P15884 label as verified, imposing fixed
      stoichiometry, or asserting that every member directly contacts every other member.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:11955446
      supporting_text: Wnt transduction is mediated by the association of beta-catenin with
        nuclear TCF DNA binding factors
    - reference_id: PMID:9065401
      supporting_text: hTcf-4 transactivates transcription only when associated with beta-catenin

- term:
    id: GO:1990909
    label: Wnt signalosome
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000107
  qualifier: part_of
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q02248
  - ensembl:ENSMUSP00000007130
  review:
    summary: 'Wnt signalosome: the specific source or functional scope remains unresolved.'
    action: UNDECIDED
    reason: The exact mouse IDA donor from PMID:22899650 is retained. Its original experiments
      identify beta-catenin in an endogenous LRRK2-containing cytosolic complex, whereas the
      membrane-recruitment and receptor-binding assays directly examine LRRK2. The signalosome
      model and the same authors’ later review (PMID:24115276) include recruitment of beta-catenin-containing
      machinery, but do not resolve which target-specific observation supports the part-of
      assertion. GO:1990909 permits additional cytosolic components, so a blanket exclusion
      of beta-catenin is unwarranted. Leave membership undecided pending clarification of
      the experimental complex boundary; absence from an inspected assay is not evidence of
      absence.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: GO_REF:0000107
    - reference_id: PMID:22899650
    - reference_id: PMID:24115276
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: UNRESOLVED
      source_entities:
      - source_id: UniProtKB:Q02248
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: Resolved accession Q02248. Exact records 417244862; references PMID:22899650.
          Literal extensions retained; source experiments are not all claimed as personally
          read.
- term:
    id: GO:1990909
    label: Wnt signalosome
  evidence_type: NAS
  original_reference_id: PMID:24115276
  qualifier: part_of
  review:
    summary: 'Wnt signalosome: the specific source or functional scope remains unresolved.'
    action: UNDECIDED
    reason: The NAS review presents beta-catenin recruitment in an LRRK2/Wnt-receptor model.
      The corresponding original co-immunoprecipitation supports a cytosolic LRRK2–beta-catenin/destruction-complex
      association, while receptor-membrane experiments concern LRRK2. These data do not settle
      direct beta-catenin membership in the receptor-associated Wnt signalosome. The term
      definition does not exclude beta-catenin categorically; retain the positive association
      and leave this complex assignment unresolved.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:24115276
- term:
    id: GO:2000008
    label: regulation of protein localization to cell surface
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:19996314
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: 'regulation of protein localization to cell surface: retain the positive contextual
      association or function.'
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The original HMEC-1 experiments recover TRPC4 with beta-catenin and show contact-dependent
      junctional targeting. In HEK293 reconstitution, beta-catenin expression promotes TRPC4-dependent
      calcium entry in contact-forming cells but retains channel intracellularly in isolated
      cells. Preserve this conditional association/targeting role. Mouse TRPC4 constructs,
      human cell hosts and the authors’ unresolved possibility of additional bridging scaffolds
      are distinct; the assays do not establish a purified binary interaction.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:19996314

- id: PMID:11130075
  title: Adherens junctions and beta-catenin-mediated cell signalling in a non-metazoan organism.
  findings:
  - statement: A beta-catenin-related armadillo protein acts both at junctions and in signalling
      in a non-animal.
    supporting_text: We have isolated a gene encoding a beta-catenin homologue, aardvark,
      which is a component of the junctional complex, and, independently, is required for
      cell signalling
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Abstract only. Discovery of actin-associated intercellular junctions in
      Dictyostelium and of Aardvark, a beta-catenin homologue that is a junctional component
      and is independently required for signalling.
- id: PMID:21393547
  title: A polarized epithelium organized by beta- and alpha-catenin predates cadherin and
    metazoan origins.
  findings:
  - statement: Catenin-based epithelial polarity predates Wnt signalling and classical cadherins.
    supporting_text: the role of the catenins in cell polarity predates the evolution of Wnt
      signaling and classical cadherins
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Full text cached. Dictyostelium alpha-catenin binds Aardvark; both are required
      for a polarized tip epithelium; no cadherin homolog in Dictyostelium.
- id: PMID:22837400
  title: Origin of metazoan cadherin diversity and the antiquity of the classical cadherin/β-catenin
    complex.
  findings:
  - statement: Sponge beta-catenin retains the residues needed for E-cadherin binding.
    supporting_text: Oc_bcat has two lysine residues (homologous to positions K312 and K435
      in mouse) required for the interaction of mouse β-catenin with E-cadherin
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Full text cached. Classical cadherins appear with animals; sponge beta-catenin
      conserves cadherin-binding residues and a Y2H screen recovered the sponge classical
      cadherin.
- id: PMID:20883218
  title: Structure and expression of conserved Wnt pathway components in the demosponge Amphimedon
    queenslandica.
  findings:
  - statement: Wnt-pathway components are largely absent from non-animal genomes.
    supporting_text: Most of these genes are not detected in the choanoflagellate and other
      nonmetazoan eukaryotic genomes
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Abstract only. Amphimedon has core Wnt-beta-catenin pathway genes, most
      of which are not detected outside animals.
- id: PMID:14647383
  title: An ancient role for nuclear beta-catenin in the evolution of axial polarity and germ
    layer segregation.
  findings:
  - statement: Nuclear beta-catenin patterning function is ancient within animals.
    supporting_text: translocated into nuclei in cells at the site of gastrulation and used
      to specify entoderm
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Abstract only. Nuclear beta-catenin specifies endoderm in the cnidarian
      Nematostella.
- id: PMID:29848444
  title: Gene family innovation, conservation and loss on the animal stem lineage.
  findings:
  - statement: Beta-catenin is an animal-specific gene family.
    supporting_text: this set of genes includes seven from the Wnt pathway (including Frizzled,
      Dishevelled, TCF/LEF and β-catenin)
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Full text cached. Lists catenin beta among the core gene families that arose
      on the animal stem lineage.
- id: PMID:23481191
  title: New insights into the evolution of metazoan cadherins and catenins.
  findings:
  - statement: ARM repeats are older than animals.
    supporting_text: the cadherin repeat domain and the armadillo repeat domain, predate metazoans
  reference_review:
    relevance: LOW
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: 'Abstract only. Review: the armadillo repeat domain predates animals, but
      catenin family diversity is metazoan.'
- id: PMID:12128211
  title: Loss of the beta-catenin homologue aardvark causes ectopic stalk formation in Dictyostelium.
  findings:
  - statement: Aardvark has cytoskeletal and signalling roles in Dictyostelium development.
    supporting_text: Aardvark (Aar) is a Dictyostelium beta-catenin homologue with both cytoskeletal
      and signal transduction roles during development
  reference_review:
    relevance: LOW
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Abstract only. Loss of aardvark causes ectopic stalks in Dictyostelium;
      the phenotype does not involve GSK-3.
- id: PMID:29880641
  title: Analysis of a vinculin homolog in a sponge (phylum Porifera) reveals that vertebrate-like
    cell adhesions emerged early in animal evolution.
  findings:
  - statement: Sponge vinculin does not bind beta-catenin.
    supporting_text: Moreover, Op vinculin bound talin but not β-catenin
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Full text cached. Sponge vinculin bound talin but not a sponge beta-catenin
      peptide.
- id: file:human/CTNNB1/CTNNB1-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md
  title: CTNNB1 beta-catenin family taxonomic census (UniProt/PANTHER)
  findings:
  - statement: PANTHER PTHR45976 has 4921 metazoan and 2 non-metazoan (likely contaminant
      plant) UniProt entries, none in choanoflagellates, filastereans, ichthyosporeans or
      Dictyostelium; Aardvark Q54I71 is classified in PTHR22895.
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Local computed UniProt/PANTHER/InterPro taxonomic census verifying that
      the beta-catenin family is effectively metazoan-restricted in current HMM classifications,
      while Dictyostelium Aardvark is classified in PTHR22895 rather than the CTNNB1 family.

  title: Inhibition of Wnt signaling by ICAT, a novel beta-catenin-interacting protein.

    review_notes: Complete cached Results/Discussion identify ICAT as an inhibitor and beta-catenin

- id: PMID:19340315
  title: HD-PTP is a catalytically inactive tyrosine phosphatase due to a conserved divergence
    in its phosphatase domain.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Actual Methods/Results/Discussion report negative wild-type HD-PTP/PTPN23

- id: PMID:22899650
  title: LRRK2 functions as a Wnt signaling scaffold, bridging cytosolic proteins and membrane-localized
    LRP6.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected original evidence supports a cytosolic LRRK2–beta-catenin/destruction-complex
      association; membrane/receptor experiments concern LRRK2. Direct beta-catenin membership
      in the Wnt signalosome remains unresolved.
- id: PMID:29066500
  title: Suppression of protein tyrosine phosphatase N23 predisposes to breast tumorigenesis
    via activation of FYN kinase.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Selected original Methods/Results report bacterial wild-type PTPN23 domain

      partner catalytic class, not a demonstrated CTNNB1 substrate reaction.
- id: PMID:30024850
  title: The major β-catenin/E-cadherin junctional binding site is a primary molecular mechano-transductor
    of differentiation in vivo.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Independent original reading establishes a force-responsive beta-catenin/cadherin
      interface through mouse-structure simulations and fly FRET/FLIM, force rescue, accessibility
      and FRAP. Application to conserved human Y654 is an explicit inference, not a human
      or muscle experiment.
- id: PMID:32591542
  title: The receptor PTPRU is a redox sensitive pseudophosphatase.
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: Genuine later original PTPRU structural/enzymatic evidence establishes pseudophosphatase
      domains for Q92729. This qualifies the older catalytic interpretation without negating
      recovered beta-catenin association.

- id: PMID:41264553
  title: 'Editorial Note: Global Regulator SATB1 Recruits β-Catenin and Regulates TH2 Differentiation
    in Wnt-Dependent Manner.'
  findings: []
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: The editorial notice is retained as source-quality context for PMID:20126258.
      It is assessed with the original and earlier notice, not used as a new CTNNB1 functional

core_functions:
- description: Wnt-responsive transcriptional coactivation in the nucleus. Beta-catenin binds
    TCF/LEF factors and participates in chromatin-associated complexes with BCL9/PYGO, CBP/p300
    and other coregulators. Its activation regions support transcription without intrinsic
    sequence-specific DNA-binding activity. It can dock onto preassembled coregulator scaffolds;
    the composition and recruitment order vary with context.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0003713
    label: transcription coactivator activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0060070
    label: canonical Wnt signaling pathway
  - id: GO:0045944
    label: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005634
    label: nucleus
  in_complex:
    id: GO:1990907
    label: beta-catenin-TCF complex
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:11751639
    supporting_text: beta-catenin, a dedicated coactivator of LEF/TCF enhancer-binding proteins
  - reference_id: PMID:9065401
    supporting_text: hTcf-4 transactivates transcription only when associated with beta-catenin
  - reference_id: PMID:17052462
    supporting_text: Stimulation of the Wnt pathway leads to the association of beta-catenin
      with Tcf and BCL9 in the nucleus
- description: Cadherin-tail binding and recruitment of alpha-catenin at adherens junctions.
    Beta-catenin provides a structural connection within the cadherin–catenin complex that
    supports cadherin retention, junction assembly and cell-cell adhesion. Alpha-catenin supplies
    the regulated actin-associated interface; beta-catenin is not assigned its partner’s actin-binding
    activity.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0045296
    label: cadherin binding
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0044331
    label: cell-cell adhesion mediated by cadherin
  - id: GO:0034333
    label: adherens junction assembly
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005912
    label: adherens junction
  in_complex:
    id: GO:0016342
    label: catenin complex
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:11713476
    supporting_text: The multifunctional protein beta-catenin is important for cell adhesion,
      because it binds cadherins
  - reference_id: PMID:18287330
    supporting_text: linking the VE-cadherin junction complex to the cytoskeleton
  - reference_id: PMID:18593713
    supporting_text: Smad7 increases the stabilized beta-catenin to form a complex with E-cadherin
      and stabilizes the E-cadherin-beta-catenin complex
  - reference_id: PMID:22837400
    supporting_text: Oc_bcat has two lysine residues (homologous to positions K312 and K435
      in mouse) required for the interaction of mouse β-catenin with E-cadherin
- description: Binding alpha-catenin through the N-terminal region recruits the catenin-complex
    alpha subunit to the cadherin-associated junctional machinery. This distinct binding activity
    complements cadherin-tail recognition by the armadillo-repeat region and supports the
    regulated connection of the junction to the actin cytoskeleton. Alpha-catenin supplies
    the actin-associated interface; this core does not assign direct actin-binding activity
    to beta-catenin.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0045294
    label: alpha-catenin binding
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005912
    label: adherens junction
  in_complex:
    id: GO:0016342
    label: catenin complex
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:7890674
    supporting_text: although the amino-terminal half independently binds alpha-catenin
  - reference_id: PMID:9264463
    supporting_text: Here we have now identified the reciprocal complementary binding site
      in alpha-catenin which mediates its interaction with beta-catenin and plakoglobin
suggested_questions:
- question: Can the TCF4 interaction records be reconciled at clone/accession level between
    E2-2 (P15884) and TCF7L2 (Q9NQB0), preserving the originally curated partner while resolving
    historical aliases?
- question: Which below-quantification beta-catenin PDZ-screen records represent reproducible
    weak interactions, and which positive alternate-domain measurements can be validated with
    the exact native protein products?
- question: Does beta-catenin make an experimentally separable contribution to hippocampal
